Definition: to sate, i.e. fill to satisfaction (literally or figuratively)
BiblicalUsage: The Hebrew word sâbaʻ means to sate, that is fill to satisfaction (literally or figuratively). In 1 Chronicles 23:1, we read, "So when David was old and full of…"; in 2 Chronicles 24:15, "…Jehoiada waxed old, and was full of days…". You hear it again in Amos 4:8 — "…cities wandered unto one city, to drink water…" — and in Deuteronomy 6:11, "…houses full of all good, which thou filledst…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sâbaʻ matters because God chose this word, and it tells the truth about how God deals with his people. I believe sâbaʻ is still true for us, because the God who gave it has not changed his mind.
